answer: Behavioural Thread Consistency rule: each identity's actions are hashed into a per-epoch behavioural thread, and reputation flows only along edges where consecutive epochs stay correlated above a threshold. A new identity starts with a sparse plume of low-weight history, so sudden high-value activity is discounted until correlation accumulates. Enforced against a shared trellis of cross-epoch checkpoints, splitting into many fresh identities pays the full correlation-building cost per sybil, since each must independently sustain consistent behaviour across epochs before gaining weight.
